newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish tennis ace Borg faces bankruptcy action.
newsitem.headline: Swedish tennis ace Borg faces bankruptcy action.

text.p: Creditors of former Swedish tennis superstar Bjorn Borg said on Wednesday they were seeking to have Borg declared bankrupt.
A group of 11 creditors, who are owed about 10 million crowns ($1.5 million) from one of Borg's companies that collapsed in 1989, said they had grown tired of waiting for payment.

Lawyer Bertil Sodermark, who represents the creditors, said Borg had not made any attempt to pay off his debts despite court rulings in 1992, 1993 and 1994 which rejected arguments that he was not personally liable and ordered him to pay up.
Borg hasn't fulfilled his promises to make arrangements to pay up and so now we want to raise the temperature," Sodermark told Reuters.
No-one was available to comment on Borg's behalf.
Borg, who turned 40 this summer, branched out into business after retiring from centre court in the early 1980s, ploughing his winnings into fashion and design.
The former player, who became the heartthrob of Wimbledon with his shaggy, shoulder-length blond hair and headband, still holds the record as five times Wimbledon champion.
But Borg's business ventures were a flop -- mirroring his personal life as he divorced his second wife, Italian Loredana Berte, and admitted in a 1992 television interview to taking cocaine.
Amid massive debts, his companies Bjorn Borg Invest AB and Bjorn Borg Enterprises Ltd collapsed in 1989 and were declared bankrupt in 1990.
Sodermark said creditors owed money by Bjorn Borg Invest have applied to put Borg into bankruptcy, which will force Borg to reveal his personal financial dealings to the court.

Sodermark said there had never been a full investigation into Borg's affairs, including his link to Dutch company Gavo NV which holds the licence for Bjorn Borg clothing and fashion accessories that is sold in stores internationally.
Borg's parents are members of Gavo's board of directors.

Gavo in turn is owned by a company called Arom Investment LV which is registered in the Dutch Antilles in the West Indies. Borg himself is on the board of this company alongside his parents, Sodermark said.
"Borg can earn a lot of money just by using his name," Sodermark said. "We think he should pay some of this money to his creditors."
